summary: Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is a scholar in Indology and the history of archaeology. He studied under Kim Plofker and completed his doctorate in 2008 under the supervision of David Pingree.

Tokio Takata is a sinologist, linguist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and EPHE, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1997–2014) and Fudan University (2016–2022), and as researcher at Toyo Bunko.

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and lecturer at Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He taught at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and as a lecturer at Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nishida, Husserl, and Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University (1925–1943), Kyoto University (1931–1953), and Ryukoku University (1961), and was president of Kyoto University of Education.
Tom De Rauw is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate under the supervision of Ann Heirman. He held an AAP position at Ghent University, attested in 2026.

Tom Ginsburg is a legal and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of California, Berkeley. He was affiliated with the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before becoming a distinguished service professor of law and political science at the University of Chicago (~2008).

Tom Hannes is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Antwerp and a master's from KU Leuven, later working as a postdoctoral researcher at Eindhoven University of Technology in 2020.

Tom Tillemans is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May. He served as emeritus professor of Buddhist studies at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and held a visiting chair at the University of Calgary (~2005).
Tomohiro Manabe is an Indologist and philosopher. He held a lecturer position at Waseda University (attested 2020) and an associate professorship at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa is a scholar of religious studies and history. She studied at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara. Masuzawa served on the faculty at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999).

Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an appointment as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012) and as a professor at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a post as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He later served as a part-time lecturer there (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a special research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and as an associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Madras and Banaras Hindu University under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal. He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, William Sax, and Jim Wilson. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2009).

Toni Schmid (1897–1972) was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at the universities of Vienna, Lund, and Uppsala under Helmer Smith. From 1944 to 1968, she served as an extraordinary antiquarian at the Royal Swedish Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities.

Tony K. Stewart is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Western Kentucky University. He taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and held a post at Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Tony Walter is a sociologist of religion who studied at Durham University and the University of Aberdeen. He held posts at the University of Aberdeen (1970–1974), the University of Reading (1994–2006), and the University of Bath as professor (2006) and emeritus.
